subject: Problems with initial values in JAGS but not in WinBUGS

messages.author: 6df91b78d5b3b587
messages.subject: Problems with initial values in JAGS but not in WinBUGS
parts:
Dear HMEcology group,

I'm running a dynamic site-occupancy HM with data of mosquito presence. Data were  vectorized (nrow= nobservations) and initial values of z were in a matrix (nrow= nsites, ncol= n_primary_periods). I'm testing two different sets of initial values:
1) a given site and primary period had z=1 if mosquitoes were detected in at least one secondary period;
2) a given site had z=1 for all primary periods after the first detection of mosquitoes.

The analysis runs fine in WinBugs while in JAGS I have the following error: 
"Error in jags.model(file = model.file, data = data, inits = inits, n.chains = n.chains,  : 
  Error in node y[5769]
Node inconsistent with parents"

I've done several tests (with default initial values, initial values in a vectorized format, initial values for other parameters [gamma,epslon]) and I'm pretty sure the error is due to  different ways that JAGS and WINBUGS deal with initial values.
Do you have any clue why JAGS is more demanding than WINBUGS considering initial values ? 

Cheers

--


André Luís Luza

Pesquisador de Pós-Doutorado
Programa de Pós-Graduação em Ecologia 
Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul

messages.author: ecb9dc91d7ca3aa8
messages.subject: Re: Problems with initial values in JAGS but not in WinBUGS
parts:
André,

Have you tried setting all values in z to 1? If I understand correctly, z is your latent state matrix. JAGS can be quite picky about those if initial values of the hyper parameters (flat priors I assume) do not lead to probabilities that are in line with the values in z.

HTH,

Peter

--

messages.subject: RE: Problems with initial values in JAGS but not in WinBUGS
parts:
Andre,

I’ve run lots of occupancy models in jags, and the thing is if there is a 1 in the initial values where there isn’t a 1 in the data, you will get that error every time. Basically, your initial values should match your detection data or it won’t work. For example, if y[i, ] = 0  1  0, the initial z value should be 1 but if y[i, ] = 0  0  0 the initial value has to be 0.

 

It works the same as you start aggregating up. WinBUGS doesn’t have this issue.

 

Incidentally, it’s the same with N-mixture models where the initial values need to match the counts.

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: Problems with initial values in JAGS but not in WinBUGS
parts:
Dear Andre, Andrew, Peter, et al.

Andrew: I think you meant the other way round: if you initialize a z at 0 when there is a 1 in the data for the same time point, then this represents a contradiction between model, data and inits and JAGS will crash (it wouldn't be a contradiction in a model that allows false positives).

Normally you can initialize the z's for standard occupancy models (i.e., with false-negatives only) with 1's for everybody and that should work. Have you tried that, Andre ? Although you have an autologistic model and perhaps that makes things more difficult?

Perhaps you can run the model in WinBUGS for a couple 100 iterations and then take the estimates from that as inits for another run in JAGS ? Or: if the model runs in good old WinBUGS, avoid JAGS altogether ?

Best regards  ---- Marc

PS: And I have no clue for why JAGS is so picky with its inits. For some more complicated models this pickiness may make JAGS almost useless, because you may be unable to get any set of inits that avoids such data/model/inits contradictions.

Dear Andre, Andrew, Peter, et al.

Andrew: I think you meant the other way round: if you initialize a z at 0 when there is a 1 in the data for the same time point, then this represents a contradiction between model, data and inits and JAGS will crash (it wouldn't be a contradiction in a model that allows false positives).

Normally you can initialize the z's for standard occupancy models (i.e., with false-negatives only) with 1's for everybody and that should work. Have you tried that, Andre ? Although you have an autologistic model and perhaps that makes things more difficult?

Perhaps you can run the model in WinBUGS for a couple 100 iterations and then take the estimates from that as inits for another run in JAGS ? Or: if the model runs in good old WinBUGS, avoid JAGS altogether ?

Best regards  ---- Marc

PS: And I have no clue for why JAGS is so picky with its inits. For some more complicated models this pickiness may make JAGS almost useless, because you may be unable to get any set of inits that avoids such data/model/inits contradictions.
From: hmec...@googlegroups.com [hmec...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of Andy Crosby [cro...@ualberta.ca]
Sent: 24 October 2018 20:57
To: Peter Solymos; luza....@gmail.com
Cc: hmec...@googlegroups.com
Subject: RE: Problems with initial values in JAGS but not in WinBUGS

Andre,

I’ve run lots of occupancy models in jags, and the thing is if there is a 1 in the initial values where there isn’t a 1 in the data, you will get that error every time. Basically, your initial values should match your detection data or it won’t work. For example, if y[i, ] = 0  1  0, the initial z value should be 1 but if y[i, ] = 0  0  0 the initial value has to be 0.

 

It works the same as you start aggregating up. WinBUGS doesn’t have this issue.

 

Incidentally, it’s the same with N-mixture models where the initial values need to match the counts.

Hi all,

One more idea of how to initialize the z vector/matrix in jags is to initialize it as 1 for all sites where the species was detected, and set to NA for all other sites:

z <- ifelse(y > 0, 1, NA)  # (in this example, the surveys are aggregated into binomial data)

I then include the z vector/matrix as one of the data inputs:
jags_data <-  list("y", "z", ...)

Cheers,
Kristin

Andrew: I think you meant the other way round: if you initialize a z at 0 when there is a 1 in the data for the same time point, then this represents a contradiction between model, data and inits and JAGS will crash (it wouldn't be a contradiction in a model that allows false positives).

Normally you can initialize the z's for standard occupancy models (i.e., with false-negatives only) with 1's for everybody and that should work. Have you tried that, Andre ? Although you have an autologistic model and perhaps that makes things more difficult?

Perhaps you can run the model in WinBUGS for a couple 100 iterations and then take the estimates from that as inits for another run in JAGS ? Or: if the model runs in good old WinBUGS, avoid JAGS altogether ?

Best regards  ---- Marc

PS: And I have no clue for why JAGS is so picky with its inits. For some more complicated models this pickiness may make JAGS almost useless, because you may be unable to get any set of inits that avoids such data/model/inits contradictions.

Andre,

I’ve run lots of occupancy models in jags, and the thing is if there is a 1 in the initial values where there isn’t a 1 in the data, you will get that error every time. Basically, your initial values should match your detection data or it won’t work. For example, if y[i, ] = 0  1  0, the initial z value should be 1 but if y[i, ] = 0  0  0 the initial value has to be 0.

 

It works the same as you start aggregating up. WinBUGS doesn’t have this issue.

 

Incidentally, it’s the same with N-mixture models where the initial values need to match the counts.

Have you tried setting all values in z to 1? If I understand correctly, z is your latent state matrix. JAGS can be quite picky about those if initial values of the hyper parameters (flat priors I assume) do not lead to probabilities that are in line with the values in z.

Dear HMEcology group,

 

I'm running a dynamic site-occupancy HM with data of mosquito presence. Data were  vectorized (nrow= nobservations) and initial values of z were in a matrix (nrow= nsites, ncol= n_primary_periods). I'm testing two different sets of initial values:

1) a given site and primary period had z=1 if mosquitoes were detected in at least one secondary period;

2) a given site had z=1 for all primary periods after the first detection of mosquitoes.

 

The analysis runs fine in WinBugs while in JAGS I have the following error: 

"Error in jags.model(file = model.file, data = data, inits = inits, n.chains = n.chains,  : 

  Error in node y[5769]

Node inconsistent with parents"

 

I've done several tests (with default initial values, initial values in a vectorized format, initial values for other parameters [gamma,epslon]) and I'm pretty sure the error is due to  different ways that JAGS and WINBUGS deal with initial values.

Do you have any clue why JAGS is more demanding than WINBUGS considering initial values ?
